active_params_definition: Backbone per-token compute parameters: all attention (including the delta v1.5 Mla indexer and the SWA branch, whose dedicated MLA K/V projections are per-token compute; the KDA window adds no matrix parameters because it shares the delta-rule q/k/v) + dense layer-0 MLP + per LatentMoE layer (latent projections, router, top-2 routed experts, all shared experts) + norms and AttnRes. Excludes the tied embedding (a lookup, not per-token compute), the ViT (active on image tokens only) and the MTP auxiliary head (training-only, dropped at inference).
deviations: LatentMoE expert counts and sizes are ours (scale-down): 12 routed + 2 shared with top-2 dispatch, latent 768 (0.5 x hidden, as the base's 3584/7168), expert intermediate 384; the base runs 896 routed experts with 16 active (kda-formulas.md :421-424), so only the qualitative proportions carry over (MODEL-L3-SKELETON.md section 1).

QB (Eq. 14, kda-formulas.md :578-583) required interpretation: the per-token cutoff alpha_i^{(t)} — 'cutoff from Top-(k+1) routing' (:558-561) — is taken as the (k+1)-th largest dispatch score s_i + b of token i, and the quantile runs over the raw sigmoid scores s_{:,j} - alpha exactly as written; the update replaces b every step (no momentum or damping is disclosed). The histogram over all-reduced marginals (:592-598) is replaced by an exact batch quantile at skeleton scale.

The QB load-imbalance loss (n * sum_j f_j * P_j over hard dispatch fractions f and mean mixture weights P, weight qb_weight = 0.01, averaged over MoE layers) is ours: the paper's QB is a non-gradient bias update (Eq. 14) and defines no differentiable loss. We add the standard load-balancing form as a *monitoring* term with its gradient stopped — the router is trained only by the NTP/MTP loss, since a differentiable aux loss empirically destabilises the tiny smoke model.

active_params_per_token (~0.47B) exceeds the ~0.25-0.35B orientation of MODEL-L3-SKELETON.md section 1: attention alone is ~277M and the frozen design fixes the dense layer-0 MLP (~19M), so the band is unreachable without changing attention or the full-width shared path; the total stays inside the 0.9-1.2B budget.

Shared experts use the same SiTU-GLU intermediate (384) as routed experts on the full-width path; the base discloses only that shared experts are full-width (kda-formulas.md :421-424), not their intermediate width.

AttnRes is integrated additively (h_l = h_{l-1} + f_l + r_l) and uses the full form (Eq. 8-9); the report's block form is the 93-layer case, and its own text assigns the full form to L<100. The additive-vs-replacing semantics are not pinned by the source.

The ViT-S vision encoder keeps learned 2D positional embeddings; NoPE applies to the language backbone (KDA/MLA) per K3 :781, not to the vision encoder's spatial layout (the source does not state the ViT drops position embeddings).
Per-head Muon weight-clip magnitude is our value (exact MuonClip bound not disclosed in K3).
Curriculum split 90/10 is our constant (the long-sequence fraction is not disclosed).
MTP auxiliary-loss weight lambda_mtp = 0.1 is our value (not disclosed).
KDA chunked form is implemented via an associative scan over the delta-rule transition monoid (provably equal to the recurrence); the paper's UT transform and the Pallas kernels are the L1 path.
The tokenizer's 160K vocabulary is padded with reserved tokens where the skeleton corpus is too small to fill 160K merges; reserved slots are standard for fixed-size vocabularies.

QAT implements the MXFP4 weight branch and, behind qat_kv_enabled, the MXFP4 latent KV branch (ADR-009 D3: E2M1 + one E4M3 scale per 16 channels, no second-level global scale, dequantised before attention; the SWA KV stays FP8). MXFP8 activations are deferred to the full run (FIDELITY section 4).

The KDA window branch shares the q/k/v already computed by the delta-rule linear layer (swa_share_kda_projections = true), adding 0 matrix parameters; the source (V4.1-Flash section 2.2) gives its SWA branch dedicated projections. This is our decision on the skeleton, not a source fact; the A/B fallback is dedicated projections (+~28M, inside the 0.9-1.2B corridor).

mla_top_k = 512 is the source's target value at 64 Q-heads and a 1M context (V4.1-Flash section 2.3); on the skeleton's 12 Q-heads it is a config parameter, effectively min(512, T), and is not calibrated to the smaller head count. mla_index_heads = 1 / mla_index_dim = 128 are scaled down from the source's 32 heads x 128 for 64 Q-heads (ADR-009 sizes 1-2 indexer heads as sufficient at 12 Q-heads).

A short dense phase before the sparse regime is allowed: the source trained sparse attention from scratch on 45T tokens (V4.1-Flash section 4.2.1), and down-scaling that recipe to the skeleton's 20B budget is not proven. The dense oracle (attn_dense_reference) is kept for exactly this A/B; the dense phase is our deviation, not the source's schedule.

Hierarchical sparse indexer (ADR-012, importing V4.1-Flash section 2.3.2): the first MLA layer (mode 'full') publishes a shared candidate pool of mla_pool_size = 16 blocks of mla_pool_block = 64 records (top-16 by blockwise max of its indexer scores), and the other five MLA layers (mode 'reindex') re-score only those 1024 pool records with their own indexer queries before taking their top_k = 512. Deviations from the source: (a) the pool width is an explicit parameter m rather than the source's 'blocks touched by the Top-512', so the reindex layers have 2x headroom over top_k; (b) only the *selection* is shared across layers — main KV and indexer K are not, because our MLA layers sit every fourth layer (KDA KDA KDA MLA) and cross-layer KV reuse over that spacing is the alternative ADR-009 rejected; (c) mode 'reuse' (the source's no-scoring mode, reusing the builder's Top-K) is implemented and declaratively available but not pinned, for the same layer-spacing reason; (d) the layout '1 Full + 5 Reindex' is our reading of the source's decoder groups (the extract states the encoder layout '1 Full + 5 Reuse' and leaves the decoder's modes unnamed). Selection stays train-aware: the pool is recomputed identically in training and inference.

Fused union assembly (criterion 16 delta, attn_fused_assembly = true): the union softmax weights are applied to each branch's gathered values in place instead of to a concatenated (B, Q, k_eff + W, H, D) value tensor, and the duplicate window mask is a scatter of the selected records into their window slots instead of a (Q, W, k_eff) pairwise compare. The selection, the score masking and the softmax are untouched, so this is the same arithmetic with a different association of the value reduction (divergence <= 1e-4, net/tests/test_13_sparse_dense_equivalence.py); the verbatim unfused leg is kept behind attn_fused_assembly = false for the A/B. The source (V4.1-Flash section 2.3) uses fused flash-style kernels; ours is a JAX-level fusion, the same class of deviation as the KDA Pallas note above. The fuse does not change the mechanism: the builder's fresh Top-K over the causal prefix and the reindex consumer stay exactly as ADR-012 declares them.

Exact top-k selection (criterion 16 delta, attn_topk_exact = false): a tiling + exact-merge selection (net/topk_exact.py) was implemented as the exact alternative to jax.lax.top_k (whose GPU lowering is a full bitonic sort of the row with an iota payload): the row is tiled, each tile is sorted and truncated to its top k, and the tiles are merged pairwise keeping the top k at each merge — the same set of records, exact by construction, with the pinned top_k count of test_17 preserved (the final merge level is a jax.lax.top_k of width mla_top_k). It is pinned OFF: measured inside the MLA stack the tiled kernel is ~15% slower than jax.lax.top_k (order-alternating A/B, tools/topk_exact_probe.py), because the tiling multiplies the per-scan-step sort/marshalling kernels while the selection as a whole is not on the stack's critical path — removing every selection (all three call sites, replaced by a gather) changes the 8K stack time by < 0.1%, while a control arm that does change the stack (swa_window = 0) shows -2.5 ms. Equivalence and edge cases: net/tests/test_18_exact_topk.py; measurements and attribution: docs/research/topk-exact-delta-2026-09-13.md.

Block-wise token merging in the MLA layers (ADR-018; borrowed from the Step-5-Preview model card, StepFun Team, 20.09.2026 — a model card, not a tech report, so the mechanism is borrowed and the training recipe is not; K3 does not disclose its long-context mechanics, hence this is our decision under AD-5). Declared as mla_block_merge = {enabled: false, block: 16} and read by net/attn_sparse.py (spine AD-9 / guard C-035: net/config.json is the switch, turning the mechanism on is not a code edit). The history is aggregated into blocks of block = 16 records before the sparse selection: one merged record per complete block (mean pooling of the main KV and of the indexer keys — the minimal honest aggregation: no new parameters, no learned gate, deterministic), the selection is the top min(top_k, T // block) blocks ranked by the merged record's own indexer score, and attention reads the merged records — which is where the indexer and top-k cost stops being paid per record. A position covered by a selected merged record is masked out of the window branch: the same duplicate rule D2 applies to single records (ADR-009), lifted to block granularity, so the union is never counted twice — and only eligible merged records mask, because the top_k ranking pads itself with ineligible blocks for early queries and a padding block that the sparse branch drops must not take the window copy of its causal prefix down with it (that prefix is the query's own block, i.e. exactly what the window covers). A block is eligible for a query only when all of its records precede it, so a partially causal block can never pool the future into a merged representation; consequently the query's own partially filled block (up to block - 1 records) remains the window branch's job — enabling the mechanism therefore requires swa_window >= block (checked in validate_config), and the window still provides the exact local copy. The mechanism stays off by default until the 64K gap measurement is green (criteria 1-7 of ADR-009, measurement method ADR-015); with the flag off the unmerged path is bit-for-bit unchanged (net/tests/test_23_block_merge.py, T-m1). mla_top_k, swa_window, the pool layout and the FP4 latent KV are not touched, and the ADR-012 candidate pool is a record-level mechanism that is *not* combined with block merging in this delta: a merged layer publishes no pool and a consumer layer then falls back to its exact full-prefix selection. Limits declared with the mechanism (ADR-018, Negative): granularity inside a block is lost — a needle that lands strictly inside a selected block is seen through its mean, not as itself — and this delta adds one more flag combination to the A4 acceptance matrix.
